REHOBOTH BEACH, Delaware -- Jacob Anthony is the owner and CEO of The Lions Den Candle Company in Rehoboth Beach, Delaware\.

Anthony makes handcrafted soy candles, diffusers, wax melts and soaps\.

He started in 2020, making candles as gifts with his new additional time working remotely\.

As the demand for his candles grew, he turned his hobby into a business with the help of his husband Tony Zacchei\.

In 2021, The Lions Den Candle Company became Jacob's full-time business\.

During the summer, The Lions Den Candle Company sells products at the Rehoboth Beach Farmer's Market and during the winter at Philadelphia's Christmas Village\.

Jacob has more than two dozen scents that can be bought on his website and at The Rehoboth Beach Farmer's Market this summer\.

# In aviation fuel, Iowa farmers are missing a unique market \| Opinion

Aug\. 1, 2026, 4:03 p\.m\. CT

- Tom Buis grew up on a farm, worked in the U\.S\. House and Senate, led the National Farmers Union, and later became the first CEO of Growth Energy\.
- He now serves as CEO of the American Carbon Alliance\.

No one should be surprised by the latest reportsshowing Iowa farm income has fallen sharply\. Commodity prices are abysmal, input costs remain high, and farm families continue to do what they've always done: Work harder, spend less, and hope next year brings better conditions\.

America's farmers have never wanted to depend on government assistance\. What they have always wanted is the opportunity to compete, innovate and sell more of what they produce\. Throughout our history, agriculture has prospered when we've opened new markets, not when we've expanded government programs\.

And the opportunity is here\. Sustainable aviation fuel, low-carbon marine fuels, and other next-generation biofuels have the potential to create billions of gallons of new demand for American ethanol\. Airlines are already signing long-term fuel agreements, and countries around the world are adopting low-carbon fuel standards\. The global shipping industry is looking for alternatives to traditional fuels\. These markets are real; they are growing, and Iowa farmers should be leading the way in supplying them\.

What’s worse, is Iowa farmers could be realizing these benefits today\.

Think about where we'd be today if the Summit carbon pipeline had stayed on its original schedule\. Iowa ethanol producers could already be supplying planes, ships, and cars with clean, renewable biofuels, and farmers would be seeing the benefits of stronger demand instead of another year of tight or negative margins\.

Four years of delay, delay, and more delay while farmers lose market opportunities that are increasingly being filled by foreign competitors\. It’s been said many times: \"If you snooze, you lose\.\" In this case, it's a travesty for Iowa farmers and our rural economy\.

Let America’s farmers do what they do best: Produce the safest, most abundant food, feed, and fiber\. Government’s role, and regulators' role, should be to allow them to compete for new markets, not hamstring them and then send them a check to make up for the markets they lose\.

This debate has never really been about one pipeline\. It's about whether Iowa intends to lead the next chapter of American agriculture or watch other states or countries seize the opportunity first\. Every major economic advancement has faced opposition, and there will always be those who oppose new infrastructure, ethanol, carbon capture, or modern agriculture itself\. But when projects that create new markets are delayed indefinitely, it isn't just private companies that lose\. It's farm families, ethanol plants, rural communities and the whole state economy\.

The greatest opportunity for rural America isn't another government handout\. It's creating new markets for the crops our farmers already grow\. That's how rural America has always prospered: not through government checks, but through innovation, investment and new customers\.

The rest of the world is moving\. The question is whether Iowa will seize this opportunity or continue allowing delay, bureaucracy and obstruction to leave our farmers behind\.

*Tom Buis grew up on a farm, worked in the U\.S\. House and Senate, led the National Farmers Union, and later became the first CEO of Growth Energy\. He now serves as CEO of the American Carbon Alliance\.*

# The Farmer Companies Raises $17 Million Series A And Names Randy Johnson CEO

By Amit Chowdhry Today at 2:04 PM

The Farmer Companies has raised $17 million in Series A financing and appointed former Dot’s Pretzels CEO Randy Johnson as chief executive officer\. Raff Ventures led the funding round, with participation from AJAX Capital Partners\. Johnson succeeds founder Adam Farmer, who will remain actively involved as chairman\.

The leadership change follows The Farmer Companies’ acquisition of WHISPS and supports its strategy of building a leading North American cheese-snacking business\.

Johnson previously led Dot’s Pretzels, increasing the company’s annual sales from $19 million to $250 million in approximately three years\. Hershey acquired the business for $1\.2 billion in 2021\.

The Farmer Companies’ portfolio includes WHISPS Cheese Crisps and an exclusive licensing partnership with Cabot Creamery to produce Cabot Creamery Popcorn\.

The company described Cabot Creamery Popcorn as the fastest-growing U\.S\. food popcorn brand among the 13 leading brands tracked by NielsenIQ\.

Proceeds from the Series A will support manufacturing partnerships, expanded national distribution and strategic acquisitions\.

Founded in 2021, The Farmer Companies acquires, builds and operates premium consumer brands, with a current focus on cheese-based snacks and related categories\.

# Whisps parent co\. taps former Dot's Pretzels exec as CEO

Courtesy of The Farmer Companies

The Farmer Companies announced the appointment of Randy Johnson as chief executive officer, succeeding founder Adam Farmer, who will remain active as chairman\. Johnson joins the company following this month’s closing of a $17 million Series A financing led by Raff Ventures, alongside Ajax Capital Partners, as The Farmer Companies accelerates its strategy to build its North American cheese snacking business through its ownership of Whisps and exclusive licensing partnership with Cabot Creamery\.

Johnson previously led Dot’s Pretzels, growing the company from $19 million to $250 million in annual sales in just three years prior to its 2021 acquisition by Hershey for $1\.2 billion\.

“Under Randy’s leadership, Dot’s Pretzels became one of the greatest success stories in snacking history\. Randy set Dot’s up for a strategic next step, and led the company through its transformational growth phase,” says Farmer\. “Bringing him on means The Farmer Companies can build toward our goal of redefining cheese snacking for the next generation\. Our business model is clear; we make the highest-quality cheese snacks with the best cheeses in the world\. Randy is leading our business to new heights\.”

The Farmer Companies’ premium cheese snacking portfolio includes Whisps, the 100% cheese crisp brand, and an exclusive licensing partnership with Cabot Creamery to produce Cabot Creamery Popcorn\. Proceeds from the Series A financing will support continued investment in manufacturing partnerships, national distribution, and strategic acquisitions, the company says\.

“Randy joining our talented team as CEO lets me focus on what I do best: finding great brands, made with premium ingredients, to create unforgettable flavors,” says Farmer\.

Johnson adds: “I'm excited to help build one of North America’s great consumer products companies\. Adam has already proven this category has room to grow\. My job is to help it scale\.”

Founded in 2021, The Farmer Companies acquires, builds, and grows consumer brands with a focus on premium snacking\. The company is currently investing in its vision to become North America’s leading premium cheese snacking company, it says, through a portfolio of owned and licensed brands, including Whisps Cheese Crisps and Cabot Creamery Popcorn\.

# Former Dot’s Pretzels CEO Randy Johnson tapped to lead The Farmer Companies

BURLINGTON, Vt\. — The Farmer Companies has announced the appointment of Randy Johnson as Chief Executive Officer, succeeding founder Adam Farmer, who will remain active as Chairman\. Johnson joins the company following this month’s closing of a $17 million Series A financing led by Raff Ventures, alongside AJAX Capital Partners, as The Farmer Companies accelerates its strategy to build North America’s leading cheese snacking business through its ownership of WHISPS® and exclusive licensing partnership with Cabot Creamery\.

Johnson previously led Dot’s Pretzels, growing the company from $19 million to $250 million in annual sales in just three years prior to its 2021 acquisition by Hershey® for $1\.2 billion\.

“Under Randy’s leadership, Dot’s Pretzels became one of the greatest success stories in snacking history\. Randy set Dot’s up for a strategic next step, and led the company through its transformational growth phase,” said Farmer\. “Bringing him on means The Farmer Companies can build toward our goal of redefining cheese snacking for the next generation\. Our business model is clear; we make the highest-quality cheese snacks with the best cheeses in the world\. Randy is leading our business to new heights\.”

The Farmer Companies’ premium cheese snacking portfolio includes WHISPS, the iconic 100% cheese crisp brand, and an exclusive licensing partnership with Cabot Creamery to produce Cabot Creamery Popcorn, the fastest-growing popcorn brand in U\.S\. Food among the top 13 brands tracked by NielsenIQ\. Both brands are built on the same foundation: award-winning cheese, premium ingredients, and exceptional flavor\. Proceeds from the Series A financing will support continued investment in manufacturing partnerships, national distribution, and strategic acquisitions\.

“Randy joining our talented team as CEO lets me focus on what I do best: finding great brands, made with premium ingredients, to create unforgettable flavors,” said Farmer\.

Johnson added: “I’m excited to help build one of North America’s great consumer products companies\. Adam has already proven this category has room to grow\. My job is to help it scale\.”

Dot’s Pretzels are snack twists sold in grocery store deli and bakery aisles\.

#### About The Farmer Companies

Founded in 2021, The Farmer Companies acquires, builds, and grows iconic consumer brands with a focus on premium snacking\. The company is currently investing in its vision to become North America’s leading premium cheese snacking company through a portfolio of owned and licensed brands, including WHISPS Cheese Crisps and Cabot Creamery Popcorn\. By combining world-class cheese partners, category-leading brands, and innovative product development, The Farmer Companies is redefining the future of cheese snacking\.

# Rising cheese snack producer hires new CEO

BURLINGTON, VT\. — The Farmer Cos\. has named Randy Johnson as its latest chief executive officer\. He will succeed the company’s founder Adam Farmer, who will transition to the role of chairman\.

Johnson joins The Farmer Cos\. from Dot’s Pretzels, helping raise its annual sales from $19 million to $250 million in three years and just before it was acquired by The Hershey Co\. in 2021, The Farmer Companies said\.

“Under Randy's leadership, Dot's Pretzels became one of the greatest success stories in snacking history\. Randy set Dot's up for a strategic next step, and led the company through its transformational growth phase,” Farmer said\. “Bringing him on means The Farmer Cos\. can build toward our goal of redefining cheese snacking for the next generation\. Our business model is clear; we make the highest-quality cheese snacks with the best cheeses in the world\. Randy is leading our business to new heights\.”

Since 2021, The Farmer Cos\. has been building a notable cheese snack portfolio that includes Whisps cheese crisps brand and the Cabot Creamery Popcorn brand, the latter of which is produced as part of an exclusive licensing agreement with Cabot Creamery and has now grown to become one of the top 13 US food brands, according to Chicago-based market research firm NielsenIQ\. The Farmer Cos\. closed $17 million of Series A financing, led by Raff Ventures and AJAX Capital Partners, in July, which will be used to support continued investment in manufacturing partnerships, national distribution and strategic acquisitions\.

Capital markets are places where people and organizations buy and sell long-term investments like stocks and bonds\. They help connect those who need money to grow or fund projects with investors looking to earn returns over time\. For investors, capital markets are important because they offer opportunities to invest, save, and grow their wealth through a variety of financial assets\.

loan syndication financial

\"As a founding member of Rabobank's loan syndication team,\"

A loan syndication is when several banks or investors team up to provide a single large loan, splitting the amount, risk and interest among them like people chipping in to buy an expensive shared item\. It matters to investors because it spreads credit exposure, affects how easily parts of the loan can be bought or sold, and signals how lenders view the borrower’s risk and pricing, which can influence market perception and secondary trading\.

debt capital markets financial

\"relationship management, debt capital markets, syndications, and wholesale banking,\"

Debt capital markets are the parts of the financial system where companies, governments and institutions raise money by issuing loans, bonds or notes that investors can buy\. Investors lend capital in exchange for regular interest payments and eventual repayment of principal, so changes in interest rates, the issuer’s ability to repay, or the amount of new debt offered can directly affect income, risk and the value of holdings—similar to deciding whether to buy someone’s IOU based on how likely they are to pay you back\.

wholesale banking financial

\"debt capital markets, syndications, and wholesale banking,\"

Wholesale banking is the part of a bank that provides large-scale financial services to companies, governments and other institutions — for example big loans, cash management, trade financing and help raising capital\. It matters to investors because these large contracts can produce steady, sizable revenue but also concentrated risk tied to the economy and credit conditions, much like a supplier whose fortunes depend on a few big wholesale customers rather than many small shoppers\.
